lonchidion-minimorsus:study:1.title: A new taxon of hybodontiform (Chondrichthyes, Elasmobranchii, Hybodontiformes) from the Late Triassic of Arizona, U.S.A., and its biostratigraphic importance within the Chinle Formation (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The species lived in the Late Triassic period.
Its type locality is the Chinle Formation in Arizona, United States.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Chinle Formation
Country: United States
Region: Arizona

facts.statement: Lonchidion belongs to the family Lonchidiidae within the extinct hybodont sharks.
facts.quote: Lonchidion is a genus of extinct hybodont in the family Lonchidiidae.

facts.statement: Lonchidion persisted until the very end of the Cretaceous, with its youngest fossils dated to the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: was among the last surviving hybodont genera, with its youngest known fossils dating to the very end of the Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: Lonchidion is thought to have been euryhaline, occurring in freshwater and brackish environments.
facts.quote: The genus has been proposed to be euryhaline, and is often found in freshwater and brackish deposits.

facts.statement: The teeth of Lonchidion are low‑crowned and likely used for grinding hard prey, indicating durophagous feeding.
facts.quote: The teeth of the genus are low crowned, and probably served to grind hard prey (durophagy).

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that Lonchidion may not be a valid genus, suggesting its teeth represent a juvenile hybodont morphology.
facts.quote: Some authors have proposed that Lonchidion is not a valid genus, and that its teeth instead represent a morphological type present among many juvenile hybodonts but that is later lost in adults.

facts.statement: Lonchidion is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The genus Lonchidion has a known fossil time range from the Carnian to the Maastrichtian (237 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Maastrichtian (237 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Lonchidion minimorsus was described as a new species in 2026 by Keeble and colleagues.
The genus Lonchidion first appears in the fossil record during the Middle Triassic Ladinian stage.
rejected.quote: The genus first appears in the fossil record during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian)
